text.brief: In August 1948 Chiang Ching-kuo arrived in Shanghai to enforce the gold yuan, a new currency that citizens had to buy with their gold and foreign cash.
text.record: The Nationalist government issued the gold yuan on August 19, 1948. It froze prices and ordered citizens to exchange their gold, silver and foreign currency. Chiang Ching-kuo arrested speculators, the price freeze broke within weeks, and the currency collapsed before the year was out.
text.reading: The regime spent its middle class to buy three months of stable prices, and the Party took the cities that followed partly on the regime's own collapse. A government that confiscates its citizens' savings in a crisis teaches them to wait for the other side.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. The Financial capability had no discipline the government could not override.
text.fix: Keep money under rules a crisis government cannot suspend, because savers who lose everything stop defending the system.
